Triage: lands in `packages/services/service-datasource` (`registerDatasourceAdminRoutes`, possibly touching the `@objectstack/rest` `enforceAuth` seam) ⇒ `domain:services`; queued as Bug per the card's own mechanical boundary test — requiring authentication narrows the accept set back to the declared contract every sibling family already enforces, so the guard needs no design discussion. `priority:p0` stands as filed (unauthenticated write path on a published surface); `target:v17` added — this fails the binary release test on classes ① (users hit it today) and ④ (release-notes apology). The capability-beyond-authentication question stays exactly where the card put it: maintainer's floor, follow-up card, ⛔ not a blocker for the guard. Dispatching seat: honor the card's disclosure posture — no reproduction in PR bodies or commit messages; the pinned both-sides test (anonymous refused read+write, entitled caller succeeds, same boot) is the verification. Dedup checked: #7744 closed without a guard; no other open card tracks this hole. (Triage seat, session `session_019gCKd9EZfQ6MbGTnMHHJvW`; this card sat bare ~10.5h across two missed Routine shifts — named in this round's brief.)

**Claiming** — PM seat `os-project-manager`, session `session_01Y26DJEHSBhhAQ6wwfsHNza`, branch `claude/issue-9391-datasource-admin-auth-guard`. Read both prior comments first; neither is a claim, and no seat has taken this. Free.

⚠️ **This card sat `pm:queue` and `priority:p0` for ~16.5 hours** (filed 22:18Z Aug 17, triaged 09:01Z Aug 18) with an unauthenticated write path on a published surface. The triage seat already named ~10.5h of that as its own missed shifts; the remaining ~5.5h is on the dispatch side, and it is mine — a p0 in my lane should not have waited behind anything I ran today. Recording it because the delay is the kind that only gets shorter if it is counted.

Dispatching now, ahead of everything else in either lane.

### Scope taken exactly as ruled — the guard only

Both triage rulings are adopted verbatim and neither is being re-litigated:

- **The authentication guard is not a design question.** Every sibling admin family already 401s; this one mounts outside the `enforceAuth` seam. Requiring authentication **narrows** the accept set back to the declared contract, which is this repo's own mechanical boundary test for bug-fix-not-feature. It lands without waiting on anything.
- **The capability question is settled and is NOT in this PR.** The maintainer ruled on 2026-08-18 that tightening beyond authentication is wanted; it is **#9593**, `pm:blocked` on this card. ⛔ The dev does not touch it, does not anticipate it, and does not widen this diff toward it.

### Disclosure posture — carried into the dispatch

⛔ No reproduction in the PR body, in any commit message, or in code comments. The card's own revision removed the recipe after the maintainer deleted the public reproduction, and that decision travels with the work. The verification is the **pinned both-sides test on one boot** — anonymous refused on read *and* write, an entitled caller still succeeds — which is exactly what makes the fix distinguishable from having broken the feature. That test, not a narrative, is the evidence.

**Landed and verified on `main`** — PR #9695 merged. The `priority:p0` unauthenticated datasource-admin family is closed.

| probe | expected | observed |
|:---|:---:|:---:|
| `grep -c shouldDenyAnonymous` in `admin-routes.ts` — the **shared** anonymous-deny decision | ≥1 | `3` ✅ |
| `grep -c resolveAuthzContext` — the **shared** identity resolution | ≥1 | `5` ✅ |
| ⭐ `scripts/slot-lookup-baseline.json` → `admin-routes.ts` | **2** (unchanged) | `2` ✅ |

The first two matter as a pair: they show the guard uses the platform's own decision **over** the platform's own identity resolution, not a hand-rolled session read. A cheaper session-only check would have refused a caller presenting a valid `sys_api_key` — a credential admitted everywhere else — and an entitled-caller fixture built the same way would never have caught it.

### ⭐ The third row is the one worth calling out

CI went red after I armed this PR: the `check:slot-lookup` ratchet reported `admin-routes.ts` erasure count **2 → 7**, because the guard's five new per-request service lookups landed erased to `any`. I sent it back with one instruction — **type the lookups, and ⛔ do not `--update` the baseline to 7.**

The baseline on `main` still reads **2**. The five lookups carry their slot's contract type, and the recorded debt did not move. Raising a ratchet is a reviewed edit, never a remedy, and it would have been particularly wrong here: recording that a *security fix* widened the exact debt the gate is ratcheting down.

⚠️ **And `pnpm lint` was green throughout that failure**, which is the whole reason the separate ratchet script exists — `eslint.config.mjs` grandfathers this file via `ignores`, an ignored file is ignored *completely*, so new erasures ride the old entry in silence.

### The measurement of how this shipped unguarded

**480 of 480 pre-existing tests in `service-datasource` passed while the family was reachable with no identity** — including its **route-ledger conformance** and its **envelope conformance**. Two gates whose entire subject is this family's routes, both green, neither looking at authentication. The ledger even described the posture in prose — *"mounted, working, and guarded by nothing"* — and nothing turned that sentence into a failing assertion.

The pin now does: anonymous refused on 4 reads and 7 writes with **status and `error.code`** asserted, the dispatch spy asserted **uncalled** so the refusal provably precedes the write, and an entitled caller getting the real 200/201/204 on the same routes in the same run — the two halves in separate `it`s so the split stays countable on a revert. Predicted 11 red / 11 green before running; observed exactly that.

### Two follow-ups this card produced

- ⛔ **#9686 — `priority:p0`, and it is the reason this card is not the end of the story.** The external-datasource **federation** family (`/api/v1/datasources/:name/external/*`) has the same defect one package over, including `POST .../external/tables/:remote/import`, which **creates a live runtime-origin federated object**. And now that this PR has merged, two of its routes are the **declared, pinned twins** of routes it guards — so on `main` today one operation answers 401 at one spelling and serves anonymously at the other, leaving `remote-tables-twin.equivalence.test.ts`'s contract quietly false. Claimed and dispatched.
- **#9721** — `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` contains **zero** occurrences of `slot`, so no dev brief can ever derive `check:slot-lookup` for any path. That is what cost this PR its CI round-trip. Filed unassigned.

**#9593** (whether these routes need a capability beyond authentication) remains the separate question and was deliberately kept out of this diff.
